item.title: Agent-Based Modelling
item.description: Agent-Based Modelling Definition Agent-based modelling (ABM) Studying a system by specifying the behaviour of its individual agents and simulating their interactions, so that the system’s behaviour emerges from them.

item.title: BDI Model
item.description: BDI Model Definition Beliefs, desires, intentions (BDI) In (symbolic) AI, multi-agent systems and philosophy of action, beliefs, desires and intentions map onto three distinct mental states and practical levels of reasoning: Informational level: what the agent believes to be the case in the world.

item.title: CAES Model
item.description: CAES Model Definition Commitments, Abilities, Expectations, Susceptibilities (CAES model; Boer and Sileno, "Anchoring Distributed Agency") Commitments: what the agent wants to achieve in the world (intent selection).

item.title: Intentional Stance
item.description: Intentional Stance Definition Intentional stance (Dennett, The Intentional Stance, 1987) Interpreting entities as agents, ascribing them beliefs, desires, intentions and enough rationality to do what they ought to do given those beliefs and desires.

item.title: Population-Based Training
item.description: Population-Based Training Definition Population-based training A multi-agent training approach that tests one policy against a population of other policies.

item.title: Self-Play
item.description: Self-Play Definition Self-play Training an agent’s policy by letting it play against itself: the same policy chooses the actions for each agent.

item.title: Actor-Critic
item.description: Actor-Critic Definition Actor-Critic Methods Actor-Critic methods are a class of Reinforcement Learning algorithms that combine both policy-based and value-based approaches.

item.title: Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C)
item.description: Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) Definition Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) A2C is an on-policy Actor-Critic algorithm that combines a parameterized policy (the actor, \pi_\theta) with a learned state-value function (the critic, \hat{V}_w).

item.title: Advantage Function
item.description: Advantage Function Definition The Advantage Function measures how much better taking a particular action is compared to the value of the state: A^\pi(s,a) = Q^\pi(s,a) - V^\pi(s) It answers: “How much does this action improve upon the average (state value)?” Intuition Positive advantage: The action ...

item.title: Agent Modelling
item.description: Agent Modelling Definition Agent modelling An agent explicitly models the policies of the other agents, so that it can condition its own action selection on their predicted behaviour and adapt when that behaviour changes.
